record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the signal-moments and other cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioAnalysis::jarqueBeraTest(): JB = N/6 (skewness^2 + excess_kurtosis^2/4) from signalMoments, p = upper-tail chi-square(2). The reference re-computes JB and p with scipy.stats.jarque_bera on the identical signal, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the signal-moments and other cases). The Jarque-Bera test is the formal, moment-based normality test: JB = N/6 (S^2 + K^2/4), chi-square(2) under the normality null. jarqueBeraTest is a NEW op (built on signalMoments) adding the formal normality test the ecosystem lacked -- the confirmatory partner of the descriptive moments, analogous to Ljung-Box for the ACF. It reproduces scipy.stats.jarque_bera BIT-FOR-BIT for both the statistic and the p-value (|diff| ~2e-14 / ~4e-18). Finding (an instructive nuance): JB=15.5 REJECTS normality (p=4.3e-4, above the 5.99 critical value) EVEN THOUGH signalMoments finds the distribution descriptively near-Gaussian (|skew|<0.5 and |exkurt|<1) -- because at N=1600 the test has enough power to detect the mild skew (-0.23) and kurtosis (+0.16). This is the same large-N phenomenon as the decisive ADF and Ljung-Box rejections; the honest lesson is that a formal normality test on a long physiological signal will almost always reject, so approximately Gaussian is a descriptive (effect-size) statement, not a test outcome. HONEST: a signal property; the reproducible content is the bit-exact test + the large-N nuance.
